The commonly practiced short form of the Rudra Mantra is **“Om Namo Bhagavate Rudraya॥”**. Its pure Sanskrit form is “ॐ नमो भगवते रुद्राय॥”. Its simple meaning is — “Om, I respectfully bow to Lord Rudra with devotion.” This mantra is dedicated to the Rudra form of Lord Shiva and has a place within the Vedic tradition of Rudra worship associated with Shri Rudram. Shri Rudram of the Krishna Yajurveda's Taittiriya Samhita, also known as Rudra Prashna or Namakam, offers salutations to the various powers and forms of Rudra. “Om” reminds us of the Pranava and Supreme Consciousness, “Namo” means bowing, reverence, and surrender, “Bhagavate” addresses the divine and majestic form of the Lord, and “Rudraya” expresses reverence offered to Lord Rudra. This mantra is sometimes known as the Ekadashakshari Rudra Mantra, although the term “Ekadasha Rudra” also refers to a separate Puranic tradition of the eleven forms of Shiva; different scriptures provide different lists of their names. Therefore, although the mantra and the Puranic concept of the eleven Rudras are related, it is not appropriate to treat them as exactly the same thing.

The name “Rudra” is the name of an ancient Vedic form of Lord Shiva and contains a remarkable combination of fierceness and compassion. In the Vedic tradition, Rudra is associated with a powerful, fierce, and fear-inspiring form, but the same Rudra is also associated with health, healing, and welfare. In Shri Rudram, salutations are offered to Rudra in many forms of existence, showing that divine power is not limited to only one peaceful or fierce form. Traditional interpretations of the word “Rudra” include the idea of one who removes suffering and pain, while another interpretation connects it with roaring or intense power. Together, these meanings help explain the deeper principle of Rudra: the very power that may appear fierce can destroy suffering, impurity, and injustice and prepare the way for a new order and welfare. The destruction associated with Rudra is not destruction merely for the sake of destruction; from a spiritual perspective, it can also symbolize the dissolution of inner bondage such as ignorance, ego, negative tendencies, and fear. Therefore, chanting “Om Namo Bhagavate Rudraya” inspires the practitioner not merely to fear the powerful form of God but to accept it as a transformative and welfare-oriented power.

In Puranic tradition, the manifestation of Lord Shiva's Rudra form is described in various ways in different stories. In some traditions, Rudra is described as a divine power emerging from the anger or austerity of Brahma, while other scriptures speak of eleven forms of Rudra. “Ekadasha Rudra” means eleven powers or forms of Rudra-Shiva, but their names and descriptions are not identical across different Puranas. These eleven Rudras are often symbolically associated with different powers of life force, transformation, prana, and dissolution present in creation. Puranic stories describe the manifestation of divine powers and the destruction of evil when adharma, ego, or demonic forces challenge the order of creation. Shiva's Rudra form becomes a symbol of protecting dharma, suppressing evil, and restoring balance in creation. Here, “destruction of demons” does not only mean defeating an external enemy; in devotional traditions it can also be understood as destroying the inner demons of desire, anger, greed, delusion, ego, and jealousy. In this way, the Puranic stories of Rudra remind the practitioner that true victory is not merely victory over external circumstances but victory over the impurities within one's own mind.

The word “Namo” in “Om Namo Bhagavate Rudraya” is extremely important because it carries the feeling of complete surrender. When a practitioner says “Namo,” they are not merely bowing to God but also expressing the intention to surrender their ego at His feet. “Bhagavate” remembers the divine, majestic, and auspicious form of the Lord, while “Rudraya” offers reverence to that form of Shiva which destroys impurity and leads consciousness toward purity. Thus, the complete meaning of the mantra can be expressed as — “O Supreme Divine Lord Rudra! I bow to Your powerful and auspicious energy; I surrender my ego, fear, suffering, and ignorance at Your feet, and bless me to move forward on the path of truth, courage, purity, and spiritual strength.” When this feeling is maintained during continuous remembrance of the mantra, chanting can become a practice of meditation and self-reflection rather than merely repetition of words. When the mind wanders, bringing attention back to the name of Rudra can help develop concentration. For this reason, the mantra is used in devotion, meditation, and Shiva worship as a simple and concise form of chanting.

The glory of the Rudra Mantra is traditionally associated with protection, inner strength, refuge during suffering, and freedom from negative influences. Devotional traditions hold that remembering Rudra gives courage to a fearful mind and allows the devotee to experience the shelter of Shiva during difficult circumstances. Some spiritual sources describe this mantra as a prayer for protection from negative energies, fear, and obstacles. Here, “negative energy” can also be understood in spiritual language as experiences such as fear, restlessness, harmful thoughts, anger, hopelessness, and disturbing mental influences. Regular chanting focuses the mind upon a sacred sound and, when performed with devotion, can provide a sense of inner stability and reassurance. Beliefs about chanting this mantra to remove planetary afflictions, fear of enemies, or physical suffering are found in various folk traditions, but such spiritual claims should not be presented as definite scientific or medical guarantees. In situations involving illness or physical suffering, mantra chanting may serve as prayer and emotional or spiritual support, but it is not a substitute for medical treatment. When this distinction is maintained, the significance of the Rudra Mantra becomes more meaningful: rather than guaranteeing that every external problem will disappear miraculously, it is a spiritual practice that awakens faith and courage within the devotee to face difficulties.

Its relationship with Shri Rudram gives the Rudra Mantra a deeper Vedic context. Shri Rudram is a famous Vedic hymn found in the Taittiriya Samhita of the Krishna Yajurveda, in which salutations are offered to Rudra in His fierce, peaceful, protective, and all-pervading forms. The feeling of offering salutations to Rudra at the beginning of Shri Rudram is closely connected with the spirit of the Rudra Mantra. Mantras such as “Namaste Rudra Manyava Uto Ta Ishave Namah | Namaste Astu Dhanvane Bahubhyam Uta Te Namah” in Shri Rudram offer salutations even to Rudra's anger, arrows, bow, and arms; one deeper meaning can be understood as a prayer that Rudra's powerful energy become peaceful, controlled, and protective. Therefore, Rudra's fierceness is not blind destructive power but controlled divine power for dharma and welfare. When a devotee remembers Rudra, they can pray for the removal of inner unrest, strength to overcome negative tendencies, and stability on the path of truth. From this perspective, the Rudra Mantra is not a mantra intended to create fear; it conveys the message of taking refuge in Shiva in the face of fear, humility in the face of ego, and inner purification in the face of impurity.

In daily life, remembering “Om Namo Bhagavate Rudraya” with a peaceful mind and devotional feeling can become a simple practice for meditation and self-reflection. Traditionally, this mantra is chanted in the morning or evening, during Shiva worship, abhishekam, or other Shaiva devotional practices; in some modern Shaiva traditions, it is also used before Rudram recitation or as an independent chant. While chanting, it is meaningful to remember its significance — “I bow to Rudra; I surrender my inner unrest, fear, and ego at His feet; O Shiva, keep me established on the path of truth and welfare.” Chanting with this feeling can inspire courage, discipline, concentration, and spiritual awareness. The fierce form of Rudra reminds us that some old and impure tendencies in life need to come to an end, while the auspicious form of Rudra teaches that after dissolution, space is created for new purity and creation. Ultimately, the true greatness of this mantra lies not in expecting an external miracle but in surrender, inner purification, fearlessness, righteous understanding, and the inward journey toward the Shiva principle. When a devotee wholeheartedly chants — “Om Namo Bhagavate Rudraya॥” — it is as though they offer all the fears and burdens of life at the feet of Lord Rudra and pray that Rudra's powerful energy destroy the darkness within and that Shiva's auspicious grace illuminate the heart with peace, wisdom, and fearlessness.

This sacred meditation description, popularly known as the Shiva Dhyana Shloka, is recited to visualize the divine form of Lord Maheshwara within the mind. Its Sanskrit text is — “ध्यायेन्नित्यं महेशं रजतगिरिनिभं चारुचन्द्रावतंसं रत्नाकल्पोज्ज्वलाङ्गं परशुमृगवराभीतिहस्तं प्रसन्नम् । पद्मासीनं समन्तात् स्तुतममरगणैर्व्याघ्रकृत्तिं वसानं विश्वाद्यं विश्वबीजं निखिलभयहरं पञ्चवक्त्रं त्रिनेत्रम् ॥” and its Gujarati form is — “ધ્યાયેન્નિત્યં મહેશં રજતગિરિનિભં ચારુચન્દ્રાવતંસં રત્નાકલ્પોજ્જ્વલાંગં પરશુમૃગવરાભીતિહસ્તં પ્રસન્નમ્ । પદ્માસીનં સમન્તાત્ સ્તુતમમરગણૈર્વ્યાઘ્રકૃત્તિં વસાનં વિશ્વાદ્યં વિશ્વબીજં નિખિલભયહરં પંચવક્ત્રં ત્રિનેત્રમ્ ॥”. Different textual traditions contain variants such as “Vishvavandyam” and “Vishvabijam”; however, the text given above is consistent with the Dhyana Shloka of the Shri Pashupatyashtaka and with Chapter 20, Verse 52 of the Vishveshvara Samhita of the Shiva Purana. This shloka asks the practitioner to meditate upon Lord Shiva not merely as a worshipped deity but as Maheshwara, the primordial cause of the entire universe, the seed of the universe, the remover of fear, and the Lord possessing five faces and three eyes. Thus, the purpose of the shloka is not merely to recite it; through each word, the practitioner creates a mental image of a particular divine aspect of Lord Shiva and stabilizes the mind in that image. The use of such a meditation verse before Shiva worship or meditation is part of the traditional practice of withdrawing the mind from external thoughts and concentrating it upon the chosen deity.

The shloka begins with the meaning **“Dhyaayet Nityam Mahesham”** — “One should always meditate upon Maheshwara.” “Mahesha” means the Great Lord, the Supreme God, the Supreme Shiva. Then comes the word “Rajatagirinibham.” “Rajata” means silver, “Giri” means mountain, and “Nibha” means resembling or appearing like. Thus, Lord Shiva is visualized as divine, radiant, pure, and peaceful like a shining silver mountain. This image creates a feeling of purity, coolness, and radiance in the mind. “Charuchandravatamsam” contains “Charu,” meaning beautiful, “Chandra,” meaning moon, and “Avatamsa,” meaning an ornament or adornment worn near the ear; thus it evokes the image of Shiva adorned with the beautiful moon. The moon is traditionally regarded as a symbol of coolness, peace, and mental serenity. The image of the moon upon Lord Shiva's head reminds the practitioner that alongside tremendous power there also exists cool compassion and peaceful consciousness. Next, **“Ratnakalpojjvalangam”** conveys the meaning of one whose limbs shine like jewels or are radiant with jewel-like ornaments. Here the practitioner is encouraged to meditate upon the divine radiance of Shiva's body. This opening section establishes within the mind a peaceful, radiant, serene, and divine image of Shiva so that meditation does not remain merely imagination but becomes a devotional practice of inner concentration.

The shloka then gives a beautiful description of Lord Shiva's four hands and the symbols held in them — “Parashu-Mriga-Vara-Abhiti-Hastam.” “Parashu” means an axe, “Mriga” means a deer, “Vara” represents the gesture of granting boons, and “Abhiti” or “Abhaya” represents the gesture that removes fear. The traditional verse describes Shiva as holding the axe and deer while displaying the boon-giving and fear-dispelling gestures. The axe can be contemplated as a symbol of the power to cut through ignorance, ego, and bondage, while the deer can symbolize the restless mind; the deer held in Shiva's hand seems to suggest that the restless mind should be brought under the control of divine consciousness. “Vara” represents Shiva as the giver of grace and blessings, while “Abhaya” reminds us of the Lord who removes fear and provides protection. Then comes “Prasannam,” meaning serene, peaceful, and compassionate. This single word gives special meaning to the entire image because although Shiva holds weapons in His hands, His face remains serene. Thus, the practitioner is reminded that His power is not for destructive anger but for dharma, protection, welfare, and inner transformation. In this way, meditation upon Shiva leads the practitioner toward a balance of strength and peace, dissolution and compassion, fearlessness and surrender.

“Padmasinam Samantat Stutam Amaraganaih” depicts Lord Shiva seated upon a lotus and praised on all sides by the hosts of gods. “Padmasina” means seated upon a lotus. In Indian spiritual traditions, the lotus is a symbol of purity and non-attachment — it grows in mud yet does not allow the mud to cling to its petals. Therefore, the inner meaning of meditating upon Shiva seated on a lotus can be understood as an inspiration for the practitioner to remain pure and steady while living in the world without becoming attached to it. “Samantat Stutam Amaraganaih” means Maheshwara being praised by the gods from all sides. This image creates the feeling of experiencing Shiva as the Lord of gods and the supreme refuge. Then comes “Vyaghra-Krittim Vasanam” — “Vyaghra” means tiger, “Kritti” means skin or hide, and “Vasana” means one who wears or is clothed in it. Thus, Lord Shiva is depicted wearing tiger skin. In Puranic and yogic traditions, the tiger can symbolize power, desire, fierceness, and untamed nature; Shiva seated upon it can inspire the practitioner to establish control over their tendencies and sensory powers. In this way, the external imagery of the meditation shloka gradually becomes an inner message for the practitioner — maintain purity of mind, control the senses, rise above attachment, and become established in divine consciousness.

The final description of the shloka identifies Lord Shiva as “Vishvadyam Vishvabijam Nikhilabhayharam.” “Vishvadya” means the primordial one, the beginning or original principle of the universe, while “Vishvabija” means the seed or root cause of the entire universe. Chapter 20, Verse 52 of the Vishveshvara Samhita of the Shiva Purana also describes Lord Shiva as the origin and seed of the universe. Here “seed” need not mean merely a physical seed of creation; it can also be understood as the original consciousness and cause underlying all existence. “Nikhilabhayharam” means the remover of all fear. When a devotee meditates upon this form of Shiva, they can develop the feeling of surrendering their fears, worries, unrest, and insecurity at the feet of the Lord. Finally, “Panchavaktram Trinetram” instructs the practitioner to meditate upon Shiva with five faces and three eyes. In different Shaiva traditions, the five-faced form of Shiva is associated with five divine faces or aspects of consciousness, while the three eyes are understood as symbols of knowledge, divine vision, and broad awareness of past, present, and future. This description reminds the practitioner that Shiva's vision is broader than ordinary human perception and that true meditation can also become a means of moving beyond limited perception toward an experience of expanded consciousness.

The mental visualization of this entire shloka can be used beautifully in meditation practice. The practitioner can sit calmly, allow the breath to become natural and steady, and then visualize Maheshwara with a radiant form like a silver mountain. The moon upon His head, divine radiance upon His body, the axe and deer in His hands, the boon-giving and fear-dispelling gestures, His serene face, lotus seat, tiger skin, five faces, and three eyes — the main essence of this meditation is gradually establishing this complete form within the mind. Connecting the mind with each symbol one by one can help reduce mental restlessness and develop the habit of concentrating upon a single divine form. While observing the deer, one may remember the restless mind; while contemplating the Abhaya gesture, one may cultivate freedom from fear; while contemplating the Varada gesture, one may cultivate grace and surrender; the moon can evoke coolness and peace; the third eye can evoke knowledge; and the tiger skin can evoke control of the senses. In this way, meditation upon the shloka does not remain merely a visualization of the deity but gradually becomes an observation of the qualities of one's own mind. By establishing Shiva's serene and fearless form within the mind, the practitioner can move toward spiritually calming inner anxiety, fear, anger, and ego. The purpose of traditional meditation verses is also to establish a mental form of the chosen deity and prepare the mind for worship.

The importance of reciting this shloka before worship, chanting, or meditation lies in the fact that it immediately connects the mind with a sacred visual image and feeling. Normally, before beginning worship, the mind may be occupied with numerous thoughts, work, worries, and surrounding activities; the slow recitation of a meditation shloka can become a way of withdrawing from this external restlessness and bringing the mind back toward the divine form. Because this shloka provides a complete mental image of Lord Shiva, it creates a focal point for meditation. In the context of the Vishveshvara Samhita of the Shiva Purana, this same description portrays Lord Shiva as radiant like a silver mountain, adorned with the moon, decorated with jewels, holding the axe and deer and displaying the boon-giving and fear-dispelling gestures, seated upon a lotus, wearing tiger skin, the origin and seed of the universe, remover of fear, five-faced and three-eyed. Therefore, this shloka is not merely poetic description but also a structured mental form for meditating upon Shiva. Regular remembrance of this form can help cultivate concentration, peace, and devotion. Rather than expecting miraculous results, it is more meaningful to emphasize regular meditation, devotional feeling, and self-observation. Meditating upon Shiva's five faces and three eyes can inspire the practitioner to broaden their vision; meditating upon the axe can inspire the cutting away of impurity; meditating upon the deer can help recognize the restless mind; and meditating upon the Abhaya gesture can inspire release from fear. In this way, a single shloka can gradually become a beautiful combination of meditation, devotion, and self-reflection.

The final spiritual message of this meditation shloka is that while meditating upon Lord Shiva, the practitioner gradually moves from the external form toward inner consciousness. At first, they visualize the radiance of a silver mountain, the moon, jewels, the axe, deer, boon-giving and fear-dispelling gestures, lotus seat, tiger skin, five faces, and three eyes; but with continued meditation, these symbols become messages for one's inner life. The moon teaches mental peace, the third eye reminds us of discrimination and knowledge, the Abhaya gesture gives fearlessness, the Varada gesture awakens compassion and surrender, the axe inspires the cutting away of ego and ignorance, and the deer teaches recognition of the restless mind. The lotus seat conveys the message of remaining unattached while living in the world, while the tiger skin can become a symbol of controlling powerful tendencies. Finally, “Vishvabija” and “Nikhilabhayahara” remind us of Shiva as the source of all existence and the supreme refuge who removes fear. Therefore, “Dhyaayennityam Mahesham...” is not merely a shloka describing the form of God; it is an invitation to a meditative journey that leads from external visualization toward inner peace, from restlessness toward concentration, from fear toward fearlessness, and from ignorance toward knowledge. When a devotee recites it with devotion and stabilizes the mind for some time in the divine form of Shiva, the mind can become more concentrated and inward before worship. The final feeling is — “I meditate upon that Maheshwara who is the origin and seed of the universe, who removes all fear, who is five-faced and three-eyed, and whose peaceful, serene, and auspicious presence may also shine within my heart.”

trayīvastu vyastaṃ tisṛṣu guṇabhinnāsu tanuṣu ।
abhavyānāmasmin varada ramaṇīyāmaramaṇīṃ
vihantuṃ vyākrōśīṃ vidadhata ihaikē jaḍadhiyaḥ ॥ 4 ॥

kimīhaḥ kiṅkāyaḥ sa khalu kimupāyastribhuvanaṃ
kimādhārō dhātā sṛjati kimupādāna iti cha ।
atarkyaiśvaryē tvayyanavasara duḥsthō hatadhiyaḥ
kutarkō'yaṃ kāṃśchit mukharayati mōhāya jagataḥ ॥ 5 ॥

ajanmānō lōkāḥ kimavayavavantō'pi jagatāṃ
adhiṣṭhātāraṃ kiṃ bhavavidhiranādṛtya bhavati ।
anīśō vā kuryād bhuvanajananē kaḥ parikarō
yatō mandāstvāṃ pratyamaravara saṃśērata imē ॥ 6 ॥

trayī sāṅkhyaṃ yōgaḥ paśupatimataṃ vaiṣṇavamiti
prabhinnē prasthānē paramidamadaḥ pathyamiti cha ।
ruchīnāṃ vaichitryādṛjukuṭila nānāpathajuṣāṃ
nṛṇāmēkō gamyastvamasi payasāmarṇava iva ॥ 7 ॥

mahōkṣaḥ khaṭvāṅgaṃ paraśurajinaṃ bhasma phaṇinaḥ
kapālaṃ chētīyattava varada tantrōpakaraṇam ।
surāstāṃ tāmṛddhiṃ dadhati tu bhavadbhrūpraṇihitāṃ
na hi svātmārāmaṃ viṣayamṛgatṛṣṇā bhramayati ॥ 8 ॥

dhruvaṃ kaśchit sarvaṃ sakalamaparastvadhruvamidaṃ
parō dhrauvyā'dhrauvyē jagati gadati vyastaviṣayē ।
samastē'pyētasmin puramathana tairvismita iva
stuvan​​ jihrēmi tvāṃ na khalu nanu dhṛṣṭā mukharatā ॥ 9 ॥

tavaiśvaryaṃ yatnād yadupari viriñchirhariradhaḥ
parichChēttuṃ yātāvanalamanalaskandhavapuṣaḥ ।
tatō bhaktiśraddhā-bharaguru-gṛṇadbhyāṃ giriśa yat
svayaṃ tasthē tābhyāṃ tava kimanuvṛttirna phalati ॥ 10 ॥

ayatnādāsādya tribhuvanamavairavyatikaraṃ
daśāsyō yadbāhūnabhṛta raṇakaṇḍū-paravaśān ।
śiraḥpadmaśrēṇī-rachitacharaṇāmbhōruha-balēḥ
sthirāyāstvadbhaktēstripurahara visphūrjitamidam ॥ 11 ॥

amuṣya tvatsēvā-samadhigatasāraṃ bhujavanaṃ
balāt kailāsē'pi tvadadhivasatau vikramayataḥ ।
alabhyā pātālē'pyalasachalitāṅguṣṭhaśirasi
pratiṣṭhā tvayyāsīd dhruvamupachitō muhyati khalaḥ ॥ 12 ॥

yadṛddhiṃ sutrāmṇō varada paramōchchairapi satīṃ
adhaśchakrē bāṇaḥ parijanavidhēyatribhuvanaḥ ।
na tachchitraṃ tasmin varivasitari tvachcharaṇayōḥ
na kasyāpyunnatyai bhavati śirasastvayyavanatiḥ ॥ 13 ॥

akāṇḍa-brahmāṇḍa-kṣayachakita-dēvāsurakṛpā
vidhēyasyā''sīd​​ yastrinayana viṣaṃ saṃhṛtavataḥ ।
sa kalmāṣaḥ kaṇṭhē tava na kurutē na śriyamahō
vikārō'pi ślāghyō bhuvana-bhaya- bhaṅga- vyasaninaḥ ॥ 14 ॥

asiddhārthā naiva kvachidapi sadēvāsuranarē
nivartantē nityaṃ jagati jayinō yasya viśikhāḥ ।
sa paśyannīśa tvāmitarasurasādhāraṇamabhūt
smaraḥ smartavyātmā na hi vaśiṣu pathyaḥ paribhavaḥ ॥ 15 ॥

mahī pādāghātād vrajati sahasā saṃśayapadaṃ
padaṃ viṣṇōrbhrāmyad bhuja-parigha-rugṇa-graha- gaṇam ।
muhurdyaurdausthyaṃ yātyanibhṛta-jaṭā-tāḍita-taṭā
jagadrakṣāyai tvaṃ naṭasi nanu vāmaiva vibhutā ॥ 16 ॥

viyadvyāpī tārā-gaṇa-guṇita-phēnōdgama-ruchiḥ
pravāhō vārāṃ yaḥ pṛṣatalaghudṛṣṭaḥ śirasi tē ।
jagaddvīpākāraṃ jaladhivalayaṃ tēna kṛtamiti
anēnaivōnnēyaṃ dhṛtamahima divyaṃ tava vapuḥ ॥ 17 ॥

rathaḥ kṣōṇī yantā śatadhṛtiragēndrō dhanurathō
rathāṅgē chandrārkau ratha-charaṇa-pāṇiḥ śara iti ।
didhakṣōstē kō'yaṃ tripuratṛṇamāḍambara-vidhiḥ
vidhēyaiḥ krīḍantyō na khalu paratantrāḥ prabhudhiyaḥ ॥ 18 ॥

haristē sāhasraṃ kamala balimādhāya padayōḥ
yadēkōnē tasmin​​ nijamudaharannētrakamalam ।
gatō bhaktyudrēkaḥ pariṇatimasau chakravapuṣaḥ
trayāṇāṃ rakṣāyai tripurahara jāgarti jagatām ॥ 19 ॥

kratau suptē jāgrat​​ tvamasi phalayōgē kratumatāṃ
kva karma pradhvastaṃ phalati puruṣārādhanamṛtē ।
atastvāṃ samprēkṣya kratuṣu phaladāna-pratibhuvaṃ
śrutau śraddhāṃ baddhvā dṛḍhaparikaraḥ karmasu janaḥ ॥ 20 ॥

kriyādakṣō dakṣaḥ kratupatiradhīśastanubhṛtāṃ
ṛṣīṇāmārtvijyaṃ śaraṇada sadasyāḥ sura-gaṇāḥ ।
kratubhraṃśastvattaḥ kratuphala-vidhāna-vyasaninaḥ
dhruvaṃ kartuḥ śraddhā-vidhuramabhichārāya hi makhāḥ ॥ 21 ॥

prajānāthaṃ nātha prasabhamabhikaṃ svāṃ duhitaraṃ
gataṃ rōhid​​ bhūtāṃ riramayiṣumṛṣyasya vapuṣā ।
dhanuṣpāṇēryātaṃ divamapi sapatrākṛtamamuṃ
trasantaṃ tē'dyāpi tyajati na mṛgavyādharabhasaḥ ॥ 22 ॥

svalāvaṇyāśaṃsā dhṛtadhanuṣamahnāya tṛṇavat
puraḥ pluṣṭaṃ dṛṣṭvā puramathana puṣpāyudhamapi ।
yadi straiṇaṃ dēvī yamanirata dēhārdha-ghaṭanāt
avaiti tvāmaddhā bata varada mugdhā yuvatayaḥ ॥ 23 ॥

śmaśānēṣvākrīḍā smarahara piśāchāḥ sahacharāḥ
chitā-bhasmālēpaḥ sragapi nṛkarōṭī-parikaraḥ ।
amaṅgalyaṃ śīlaṃ tava bhavatu nāmaivamakhilaṃ
tathāpi smartṝṇāṃ varada paramaṃ maṅgalamasi ॥ 24 ॥

manaḥ pratyakchittē savidhamavidhāyātta-marutaḥ
prahṛṣyadrōmāṇaḥ pramada-salilōtsaṅgati-dṛśaḥ ।
yadālōkyāhlādaṃ hrada iva nimajyāmṛtamayē
dadhatyantastattvaṃ kimapi yaminastat kila bhavān ॥ 25 ॥

tvamarkastvaṃ sōmastvamasi pavanastvaṃ hutavahaḥ
tvamāpastvaṃ vyōma tvamu dharaṇirātmā tvamiti cha ।
parichChinnāmēvaṃ tvayi pariṇatā bibhrati giraṃ
na vidmastattattvaṃ vayamiha tu yat tvaṃ na bhavasi ॥ 26 ॥

trayīṃ tisrō vṛttīstribhuvanamathō trīnapi surān
akārādyairvarṇaistribhirabhidadhat tīrṇavikṛti ।
turīyaṃ tē dhāma dhvanibhiravarundhānamaṇubhiḥ
samastaṃ vyastaṃ tvāṃ śaraṇada gṛṇātyōmiti padam ॥ 27 ॥

bhavaḥ śarvō rudraḥ paśupatirathōgraḥ saha mahān
tathā bhīmēśānāviti yadabhidhānāṣṭakamidam ।
amuṣmin pratyēkaṃ pravicharati dēva śrutirapi
priyāyāsmaidhāmnē praṇihita-namasyō'smi bhavatē ॥ 28 ॥

namō nēdiṣṭhāya priyadava daviṣṭhāya cha namaḥ
namaḥ kṣōdiṣṭhāya smarahara mahiṣṭhāya cha namaḥ ।
namō varṣiṣṭhāya trinayana yaviṣṭhāya cha namaḥ
namaḥ sarvasmai tē tadidamitisarvāya cha namaḥ ॥ 29 ॥

bahula-rajasē viśvōtpattau bhavāya namō namaḥ
prabala-tamasē tat saṃhārē harāya namō namaḥ ।
jana-sukhakṛtē sattvōdriktau mṛḍāya namō namaḥ
pramahasi padē nistraiguṇyē śivāya namō namaḥ ॥ 30 ॥

kṛśa-pariṇati-chētaḥ klēśavaśyaṃ kva chēdaṃ
kva cha tava guṇa-sīmōllaṅghinī śaśvadṛddhiḥ ।
iti chakitamamandīkṛtya māṃ bhaktirādhād
varada charaṇayōstē vākya-puṣpōpahāram ॥ 31 ॥

asita-giri-samaṃ syāt kajjalaṃ sindhu-pātrē
sura-taruvara-śākhā lēkhanī patramurvī ।
likhati yadi gṛhītvā śāradā sarvakālaṃ
tadapi tava guṇānāmīśa pāraṃ na yāti ॥ 32 ॥

asura-sura-munīndrairarchitasyēndu-maulēḥ
grathita-guṇamahimnō nirguṇasyēśvarasya ।
sakala-gaṇa-variṣṭhaḥ puṣpadantābhidhānaḥ
ruchiramalaghuvṛttaiḥ stōtramētachchakāra ॥ 33 ॥

aharaharanavadyaṃ dhūrjaṭēḥ stōtramētat
paṭhati paramabhaktyā śuddha-chittaḥ pumān yaḥ ।
sa bhavati śivalōkē rudratulyastathā'tra
prachuratara-dhanāyuḥ putravān kīrtimāṃścha ॥ 34 ॥

mahēśānnāparō dēvō mahimnō nāparā stutiḥ ।
aghōrānnāparō mantrō nāsti tattvaṃ gurōḥ param ॥ 35 ॥

dīkṣā dānaṃ tapastīrthaṃ jñānaṃ yāgādikāḥ kriyāḥ ।
mahimnastava pāṭhasya kalāṃ nārhanti ṣōḍaśīm ॥ 36 ॥

kusumadaśana-nāmā sarva-gandharva-rājaḥ
śaśidharavara-maulērdēvadēvasya dāsaḥ ।
sa khalu nija-mahimnō bhraṣṭa ēvāsya rōṣāt
stavanamidamakārṣīd divya-divyaṃ mahimnaḥ ॥ 37 ॥

suragurumabhipūjya svarga-mōkṣaika-hētuṃ [suravaramunipūjyaṃ svarga-mōkṣaika-hētuṃ]
paṭhati yadi manuṣyaḥ prāñjalirnānya-chētāḥ ।
vrajati śiva-samīpaṃ kinnaraiḥ stūyamānaḥ
stavanamidamamōghaṃ puṣpadantapraṇītam ॥ 38 ॥

śrī puṣpadanta-mukha-paṅkaja-nirgatēna
stōtrēṇa kilbiṣa-harēṇa hara-priyēṇa ।
kaṇṭhasthitēna paṭhitēna samāhitēna
suprīṇitō bhavati bhūtapatirmahēśaḥ ॥ 43 ॥

āsamāptamidaṃ stōtraṃ puṇyaṃ gandharva-bhāṣitam ।
anaupamyaṃ manōhāri sarvamīśvaravarṇanam ॥ 39 ॥

tava tattvaṃ na jānāmi kīdṛśō'si mahēśvara ।
yādṛśō'si mahādēva tādṛśāya namō namaḥ ॥ 41 ॥

ēkakālaṃ dvikālaṃ vā trikālaṃ yaḥ paṭhēnnaraḥ ।
sarvapāpa-vinirmuktaḥ śiva lōkē mahīyatē ॥ 42 ॥

ityēṣā vāṅmayī pūjā śrīmachChaṅkara-pādayōḥ ।
arpitā tēna dēvēśaḥ prīyatāṃ mē sadāśivaḥ ॥ 40 ॥

॥ iti śrī puṣpadanta virachitaṃ śivamahimna-stōtraṃ samāptam ॥
id5_story.id5_3:
namāmīśamīśāna nirvāṇarūpaṃ
vibhuṃ vyāpakaṃ brahmavēda-svarūpam ।
nijaṃ nirguṇaṃ nirvikalpaṃ nirīhaṃ
chidākāśa-mākāśavāsaṃ bhajē'ham ॥ 1 ॥

nirākāramōṅkāramūlaṃ turīyaṃ
girājñānagōtītamīśaṃ girīśam ।
karālaṃ mahākālakālaṃ kṛpāluṃ
guṇāgāra-saṃsārapāraṃ natō'ham ॥ 2 ॥

tuṣārādri-saṅkāśagauraṃ gabhīraṃ
manōbhūtakōṭi-prabhāsī śarīram ।
sphuranmaulikallōlinī chārugaṅgā
lasadbhāla-bālēndu kaṇṭhē bhujaṅgam ॥ 3 ॥

chalatkuṇḍalaṃ śubhranētraṃ viśālaṃ [bhṝsunētraṃ viśālaṃ]
prasannānanaṃ nīlakaṇṭhaṃ dayālum ।
mṛgādhīśa-charmāmbaraṃ muṇḍamālaṃ
priyaṃ śaṅkaraṃ sarvanāthaṃ bhajāmi ॥ 4 ॥

prachaṇḍaṃ prakṛṣṭaṃ pragalbhaṃ parēśaṃ
akhaṇḍaṃ bhajē bhānukōṭiprakāśam ।
trayī-śūla-nirmūlanaṃ śūlapāṇiṃ
bhajē'haṃ bhavānīpatiṃ bhāvagamyam ॥ 5 ॥

kalātīta-kalyāṇa-kalpāntakārī
sadā sajjanānanda-dātā purārī ।
chidānanda sandōhamōhāpahārī
prasīda prasīda prabhō manmathārī ॥ 6 ॥

na yāvadumānātha-pādāravindaṃ
bhajantīha lōkē parē vā narāṇām ।
na tāvatsukhaṃ śānti santāpanāśaṃ
prasīda prabhō sarvabhūtādhivāsam ॥ 7 ॥

na jānāmi yōgaṃ japaṃ naiva pūjāṃ
natō'haṃ sadā sarvadā dēva tubhyam ।
jarā-janma-duḥkhaughatātapyamānaṃ
prabhō pāhi śāpānnamāmīśa śambhō ॥ 8 ॥

rudrāṣṭakamidaṃ prōktaṃ viprēṇa haratuṣṭayē ।
yē paṭhanti narā bhaktyā tēṣāṃ śambhuḥ prasīdati ॥ 9 ॥

॥ iti śrīrāmacharitamānasē uttarakāṇḍē śrīgōsvāmi tulasīdāsakṛtaṃ
śrīrudrāṣṭakaṃ sampūrṇam ॥
id5_story.id5_4:
brahmamurāri surārchita liṅgaṃ
nirmalabhāsita śōbhita liṅgam ।
janmaja duḥkha vināśaka liṅgaṃ [vināśana]
tatpraṇamāmi sadāśiva liṅgam ॥ 1 ॥

dēvamuni pravarārchita liṅgaṃ
kāmadahana karuṇākara liṅgam ।
rāvaṇa darpa vināśana liṅgaṃ
tatpraṇamāmi sadāśiva liṅgam ॥ 2 ॥

sarva sugandha sulēpita liṅgaṃ
buddhi vivardhana kāraṇa liṅgam ।
siddha surāsura vandita liṅgaṃ
tatpraṇamāmi sadāśiva liṅgam ॥ 3 ॥

kanaka mahāmaṇi bhūṣita liṅgaṃ
phaṇipati vēṣṭita śōbhita liṅgam ।
dakṣasuyajña vināśana liṅgaṃ
tatpraṇamāmi sadāśiva liṅgam ॥ 4 ॥

kuṅkuma chandana lēpita liṅgaṃ
paṅkaja hāra suśōbhita liṅgam ।
sañchita pāpa vināśana liṅgaṃ
tatpraṇamāmi sadāśiva liṅgam ॥ 5 ॥

dēvagaṇārchita sēvita liṅgaṃ
bhāvai-rbhaktibhirēva cha liṅgam ।
dinakara kōṭi prabhākara liṅgaṃ
tatpraṇamāmi sadāśiva liṅgam ॥ 6 ॥

aṣṭadaḻōparivēṣṭita liṅgaṃ
sarvasamudbhava kāraṇa liṅgam ।
aṣṭadaridra vināśana liṅgaṃ
tatpraṇamāmi sadāśiva liṅgam ॥ 7 ॥

suraguru suravara pūjita liṅgaṃ
suravana puṣpa sadārchita liṅgam ।
parātparaṃ (paramapadaṃ) paramātmaka liṅgaṃ
tatpraṇamāmi sadāśiva liṅgam ॥ 8 ॥

liṅgāṣṭakamidaṃ puṇyaṃ yaḥ paṭhēśśiva sannidhau ।
śivalōkamavāpnōti śivēna saha mōdatē ॥
id5_story.id5_5:
tridaḻaṃ triguṇākāraṃ trinētraṃ cha triyāyudham ।
trijanma pāpasaṃhāraṃ ēkabilvaṃ śivārpaṇam ॥

triśākhaiḥ bilvapatraiścha achChidraiḥ kōmalaiḥ śubhaiḥ ।
tavapūjāṃ kariṣyāmi ēkabilvaṃ śivārpaṇam ॥

kōṭi kanyā mahādānaṃ tilaparvata kōṭayaḥ ।
kāñchanaṃ śailadānēna ēkabilvaṃ śivārpaṇam ॥

kāśīkṣētra nivāsaṃ cha kālabhairava darśanam ।
prayāgē mādhavaṃ dṛṣṭvā ēkabilvaṃ śivārpaṇam ॥

induvārē vrataṃ sthitvā nirāhārō mahēśvarāḥ ।
naktaṃ hauṣyāmi dēvēśa ēkabilvaṃ śivārpaṇam ॥

rāmaliṅga pratiṣṭhā cha vaivāhika kṛtaṃ tathā ।
taṭākānicha sandhānaṃ ēkabilvaṃ śivārpaṇam ॥

akhaṇḍa bilvapatraṃ cha āyutaṃ śivapūjanam ।
kṛtaṃ nāma sahasrēṇa ēkabilvaṃ śivārpaṇam ॥

umayā sahadēvēśa nandi vāhanamēva cha ।
bhasmalēpana sarvāṅgaṃ ēkabilvaṃ śivārpaṇam ॥

sālagrāmēṣu viprāṇāṃ taṭākaṃ daśakūpayōḥ ।
yajñakōṭi sahasrasya ēkabilvaṃ śivārpaṇam ॥

danti kōṭi sahasrēṣu aśvamēdhaśatakratau । [aśvamēdha śatāni cha / vājapēya śatāni cha]
kōṭikanyā mahādānaṃ ēkabilvaṃ śivārpaṇam ॥

bilvāṇāṃ darśanaṃ puṇyaṃ sparśanaṃ pāpanāśanam ।
aghōra pāpasaṃhāraṃ ēkabilvaṃ śivārpaṇam ॥

sahasravēda pāṭēṣu brahmastāpanamuchyatē ।
anēkavrata kōṭīnāṃ ēkabilvaṃ śivārpaṇam ॥

annadāna sahasrēṣu sahasrōpanayanaṃ tadhā ।
anēka janmapāpāni ēkabilvaṃ śivārpaṇam ॥

bilvāṣṭakamidaṃ puṇyaṃ yaḥ paṭhēśśiva sannidhau ।
śivalōkamavāpnōti ēkabilvaṃ śivārpaṇam ॥
id5_story.id5_6:
॥ śiva chālīsā ॥
ōṃ namaḥ śivāya

dōhā
jaya gaṇēśa girijāsuvana maṅgala mūla sujāna ।
kahata ayōdhyādāsa tuma dē-u abhaya varadāna ॥

jaya girijāpati dīnadayālā । sadā karata santana pratipālā ॥
bhāla chandramā sōhata nīkē । kānana kuṇḍala nāga phanī kē ॥

aṅga gaura śira gaṅga bahāyē । muṇḍamāla tana kṣāra lagāyē ॥
vastra khāla bāghambara sōhē । Chavi kō dēkhi nāga mana mōhē ॥

mainā mātu ki havē dulārī । vāma aṅga sōhata Chavi nyārī ॥
kara triśūla sōhata Chavi bhārī । karata sadā śatruna kṣayakārī ॥

nandī gaṇēśa sōhaiṃ tahaṃ kaisē । sāgara madhya kamala haiṃ jaisē ॥
kārtika śyāma aura gaṇarā-ū । yā Chavi kau kahi jāta na kā-ū ॥

dēvana jabahīṃ jāya pukārā । tabahiṃ dukha prabhu āpa nivārā ॥
kiyā upadrava tāraka bhārī । dēvana saba mili tumahiṃ juhārī ॥

turata ṣaḍānana āpa paṭhāyau । lava nimēṣa mahaṃ māri girāyau ॥
āpa jalandhara asura saṃhārā । suyaśa tumhāra vidita saṃsārā ॥

tripurāsura sana yuddha machāyī । tabahiṃ kṛpā kara līna bachāyī ॥
kiyā tapahiṃ bhāgīratha bhārī । puraba pratijñā tāsu purārī ॥

dānina mahaṃ tuma sama kō-u nāhīm । sēvaka stuti karata sadāhīm ॥
vēda māhi mahimā tuma gāyī । akatha anādi bhēda nahīṃ pāyī ॥

prakaṭē udadhi manthana mēṃ jvālā । jarata surāsura bhē vihālā ॥
kīnha dayā tahaṃ karī sahāyī । nīlakaṇṭha taba nāma kahāyī ॥

pūjana rāmachandra jaba kīnhām । jīta kē laṅka vibhīṣaṇa dīnhā ॥
sahasa kamala mēṃ hō rahē dhārī । kīnha parīkṣā tabahiṃ tripurārī ॥

ēka kamala prabhu rākhē-u jōyī । kamala nayana pūjana chahaṃ sōyī ॥
kaṭhina bhakti dēkhī prabhu śaṅkara । bhayē prasanna diē ichChita vara ॥

jaya jaya jaya ananta avināśī । karata kṛpā sabakē ghaṭa vāsī ॥
duṣṭa sakala nita mōhi satāvaim । bhramata rahauṃ mōhē chaina na āvaim ॥

trāhi trāhi maiṃ nātha pukārō । yaha avasara mōhi āna ubārō ॥
lē triśūla śatruna kō mārō । saṅkaṭa sē mōhiṃ āna ubārō ॥

māta pitā bhrātā saba kōyī । saṅkaṭa mēṃ pūChata nahiṃ kōyī ॥
svāmī ēka hai āsa tumhārī । āya harahu mama saṅkaṭa bhārī ॥

dhana nirdhana kō dēta sadā hī । jō kōyī jāñchē sō phala pāhīm ॥
astuti kēhi vidhi karōṃ tumhārī । kṣamahu nātha aba chūka hamārī ॥

śaṅkara hō saṅkaṭa kē nāśana । maṅgala kāraṇa vighna vināśana ॥
yōgī yati muni dhyāna lagāvaim । śārada nārada śīśa navāvaim ॥

namō namō jaya namaḥ śivāya । sura brahmādika pāra na pāya ॥
jō yaha pāṭha karē mana lāyī । tā para hōta haiṃ śambhu sahāyī ॥

raniyāṃ jō kōyī hō adhikārī । pāṭha karē sō pāvana hārī ॥
putra hōna kī ichChā jōyī । niśchaya śiva prasāda tēhi hōyī ॥

paṇḍita trayōdaśī kō lāvē । dhyāna pūrvaka hōma karāvē ॥
trayōdaśī vrata karai hamēśā । tana nahiṃ tākē rahai kalēśā ॥

dhūpa dīpa naivēdya chaḍhāvē । śaṅkara sammukha pāṭha sunāvē ॥
janma janma kē pāpa nasāvē । anta dhāma śivapura mēṃ pāvē ॥

kahaiṃ ayōdhyādāsa āsa tumhārī । jāni sakala dukha harahu hamārī ॥

dōhā
nita nēma uṭhi prātaḥhī pāṭha karō chālīsa ।
tuma mērī manakāmanā pūrṇa karō jagadīśa ॥

atha triguṇa āratī śivajī kī

jaya śiva ōṅkārā hara jaya śiva ōṅkārā
brahmā viṣṇu sadāśiva ardhāṅgī dhārā ॥ ṭēka॥

ēkānana chaturānana pañchānana rājē
haṃsānana garuḍāsana vṛṣavāhana sājē ॥ jaya॥

dō bhuja chāra chaturbhuja dasa bhuja ati sōhē
tīnōṃ rūpa nirakhatā tribhuvana jana mōhē ॥ jaya॥

akṣamālā banamālā ruṇḍamālā dhārī
chandana mṛgamada sōhai bhālē śaśidhārī ॥ jaya॥

śvētāmbara pītāmbara bāghambara aṅgē
sanakādika garuḍādika bhūtādika saṅgē ॥ jaya॥

kara madhyē sukamaṇḍala chakra triśūla dhartā
jagakartā jagabhartā jagasaṃhārakartā ॥ jaya॥

brahmā viṣṇu sadāśiva jānata avivēkā
praṇavākṣara ōṃ madhyē yē tīnōṃ ēkā ॥ jaya॥

kāśī mēṃ viśvanātha virājata nandō brahmachārī
nita uṭhi bhōga lagāvata mahimā ati bhārī ॥ jaya॥

triguṇa svāmī kī āratī jō kōyī nara gāvē
kahata śivānanda svāmī manavāñChita phala pāvē ॥ jaya॥
id5_story.id5_7:
viśvēśvarāya narakārṇava tāraṇāya
karṇāmṛtāya śaśiśēkhara dhāraṇāya ।
karpūrakānti dhavaḻāya jaṭādharāya
dāridryaduḥkha dahanāya namaśśivāya ॥ 1 ॥

gaurīpriyāya rajanīśa kaḻādharāya
kālāntakāya bhujagādhipa kaṅkaṇāya ।
gaṅgādharāya gajarāja vimardhanāya
dāridryaduḥkha dahanāya namaśśivāya ॥ 2 ॥

bhaktapriyāya [bhaktipriyāya] bhavarōga bhayāpahāya
ugrāya duḥkha [durga] bhavasāgara tāraṇāya ।
jyōtirmayāya guṇanāma sunṛtyakāya
dāridryaduḥkha dahanāya namaśśivāya ॥ 3 ॥

charmāmbarāya śavabhasma vilēpanāya
phālēkṣaṇāya maṇikuṇḍala maṇḍitāya ।
mañjīrapādayugaḻāya jaṭādharāya
dāridryaduḥkha dahanāya namaśśivāya ॥ 4 ॥

pañchānanāya phaṇirāja vibhūṣaṇāya
hēmāṅkuśāya bhuvanatraya maṇḍitāya
ānanda bhūmi varadāya tamōpayāya [tamōmayāya] ।
dāridryaduḥkha dahanāya namaśśivāya ॥ 5 ॥

bhānupriyāya bhavasāgara tāraṇāya
kālāntakāya kamalāsana pūjitāya ।
nētratrayāya śubhalakṣaṇa lakṣitāya
dāridryaduḥkha dahanāya namaśśivāya ॥ 6 ॥

rāmapriyāya raghunātha varapradāya
nāgapriyāya narakārṇava tāraṇāya ।
puṇyāya [puṇyēṣu] puṇyabharitāya surārchitāya
dāridryaduḥkha dahanāya namaśśivāya ॥ 7 ॥

muktēśvarāya phaladāya gaṇēśvarāya
gītāpriyāya vṛṣabhēśvara vāhanāya ।
mātaṅgacharma vasanāya mahēśvarāya
dāridryaduḥkha dahanāya namaśśivāya ॥ 8 ॥

vasiṣṭhēna kṛtaṃ stōtraṃ sarvarōga nivāraṇam ।
sarvasampatkaraṃ śīghraṃ putrapautrādi vardhanam ।
[śubhadaṃ kāmadaṃ hṛdyaṃ dhanadhānya pravardhanam]
trisandhyaṃ yaḥ paṭhēnnityaṃ sa hi svarga mavāpnuyāt ॥ 9 ॥

॥ iti śrī vasiṣṭha virachitaṃ dāridryadahana śivastōtraṃ sampūrṇam ॥
id5_story.id5_8:
ādau karmaprasaṅgātkalayati kaluṣaṃ mātṛkukṣau sthitaṃ māṃ
viṇmūtrāmēdhyamadhyē kvathayati nitarāṃ jāṭharō jātavēdāḥ ।
yadyadvai tatra duḥkhaṃ vyathayati nitarāṃ śakyatē kēna vaktuṃ
kṣantavyō mē'parādhaḥ śiva śiva śiva bhō śrīmahādēva śambhō ॥ 1॥

bālyē duḥkhātirēkō malalulitavapuḥ stanyapānē pipāsā
nō śaktaśchēndriyēbhyō bhavaguṇajanitāḥ jantavō māṃ tudanti ।
nānārōgādiduḥkhādrudanaparavaśaḥ śaṅkaraṃ na smarāmi
kṣantavyō mē'parādhaḥ śiva śiva śiva bhō śrīmahādēva śambhō ॥ 2॥

prauḍhō'haṃ yauvanasthō viṣayaviṣadharaiḥ pañchabhirmarmasandhau
daṣṭō naṣṭō vivēkaḥ sutadhanayuvatisvādusaukhyē niṣaṇṇaḥ ।
śaivīchintāvihīnaṃ mama hṛdayamahō mānagarvādhirūḍhaṃ
kṣantavyō mē'parādhaḥ śiva śiva śiva bhō śrīmahādēva śambhō ॥ 3॥

vārdhakyē chēndriyāṇāṃ vigatagatimatiśchādhidaivāditāpaiḥ
pāpai rōgairviyōgaistvanavasitavapuḥ prauḍhahīnaṃ cha dīnam ।
mithyāmōhābhilāṣairbhramati mama manō dhūrjaṭērdhyānaśūnyaṃ
kṣantavyō mē'parādhaḥ śiva śiva śiva bhō śrīmahādēva śambhō ॥ 4॥

snātvā pratyūṣakālē snapanavidhividhau nāhṛtaṃ gāṅgatōyaṃ
pūjārthaṃ vā kadāchidbahutaragahanātkhaṇḍabilvīdalāni ।
nānītā padmamālā sarasi vikasitā gandhadhūpaiḥ tvadarthaṃ
kṣantavyō mē'parādhaḥ śiva śiva śiva bhō śrīmahādēva śambhō ॥ 5॥

dugdhairmadhvājyayuktairdadhisitasahitaiḥ snāpitaṃ naiva liṅgaṃ
nō liptaṃ chandanādyaiḥ kanakavirachitaiḥ pūjitaṃ na prasūnaiḥ ।
dhūpaiḥ karpūradīpairvividharasayutairnaiva bhakṣyōpahāraiḥ
kṣantavyō mē'parādhaḥ śiva śiva śiva bhō śrīmahādēva śambhō ॥ 6॥

nō śakyaṃ smārtakarma pratipadagahanapratyavāyākulākhyaṃ
śrautē vārtā kathaṃ mē dvijakulavihitē brahmamārgānusārē । var brahmamārgē susārē
jñātō dharmō vichāraiḥ śravaṇamananayōḥ kiṃ nididhyāsitavyaṃ
kṣantavyō mē'parādhaḥ śiva śiva śiva bhō śrīmahādēva śambhō ॥ 7॥

dhyātvā chittē śivākhyaṃ prachurataradhanaṃ naiva dattaṃ dvijēbhyō
havyaṃ tē lakṣasaṅkhyairhutavahavadanē nārpitaṃ bījamantraiḥ ।
nō taptaṃ gāṅgātīrē vratajapaniyamaiḥ rudrajāpyairna vēdaiḥ
kṣantavyō mē'parādhaḥ śiva śiva śiva bhō śrīmahādēva śambhō ॥ 8॥

nagnō niḥsaṅgaśuddhastriguṇavirahitō dhvastamōhāndhakārō
nāsāgrē nyastadṛṣṭirviditabhavaguṇō naiva dṛṣṭaḥ kadāchit ।
unmanyā'vasthayā tvāṃ vigatakalimalaṃ śaṅkaraṃ na smarāmi
kṣantavyō mē'parādhaḥ śiva śiva śiva bhō śrīmahādēva śambhō ॥ 9॥

sthitvā sthānē sarōjē praṇavamayamarutkumbhakē (kuṇḍalē) sūkṣmamārgē
śāntē svāntē pralīnē prakaṭitavibhavē jyōtirūpē'parākhyē ।
liṅgajñē brahmavākyē sakalatanugataṃ śaṅkaraṃ na smarāmi
kṣantavyō mē'parādhaḥ śiva śiva śiva bhō śrīmahādēva śambhō ॥ 10॥

hṛdyaṃ vēdāntavēdyaṃ hṛdayasarasijē dīptamudyatprakāśaṃ
satyaṃ śāntasvarūpaṃ sakalamunimanaḥpadmaṣaṇḍaikavēdyam ।
jāgratsvapnē suṣuptau triguṇavirahitaṃ śaṅkaraṃ na smarāmi
kṣantavyō mē'parādhaḥ śiva śiva śiva bhō śrīmahādēva śambhō ॥ 11॥

chandrōdbhāsitaśēkharē smaraharē gaṅgādharē śaṅkarē
sarpairbhūṣitakaṇṭhakarṇavivarē nētrōtthavaiśvānarē । yugalē
dantitvakkṛtasundarāmbaradharē trailōkyasārē harē
mōkṣārthaṃ kuru chittavṛttimachalāmanyaistu kiṃ karmabhiḥ ॥ 12॥

kiṃ vā'nēna dhanēna vājikaribhiḥ prāptēna rājyēna kiṃ
kiṃ vā putrakalatramitrapaśubhirdēhēna gēhēna kim ।
jñātvaitatkṣaṇabhaṅguraṃ sapadi rē tyājyaṃ manō dūrataḥ
svātmārthaṃ guruvākyatō bhaja mana śrīpārvatīvallabham ॥ 13॥

paurōhityaṃ rajanicharitaṃ grāmaṇītvaṃ niyōgō
māṭhāpatyaṃ hyanṛtavachanaṃ sākṣivādaḥ parānnam ।
brahmadvēṣaḥ khalajanaratiḥ prāṇināṃ nirdayatvaṃ
mā bhūdēvaṃ mama paśupatē janmajanmāntarēṣu ॥ 14॥

āyurnaśyati paśyatāṃ pratidinaṃ yāti kṣayaṃ yauvanaṃ
pratyāyānti gatāḥ punarna divasāḥ kālō jagadbhakṣakaḥ ।
lakṣmīstōyataraṅgabhaṅgachapalā vidyuchchalaṃ jīvitaṃ
tasmāttvāṃ śaraṇāgataṃ śaraṇada tvaṃ rakṣa rakṣādhunā ॥ 15॥ tasmānmāṃ

vandē dēvamumāpatiṃ suraguruṃ vandē jagatkāraṇaṃ
vandē pannagabhūṣaṇaṃ mṛgadharaṃ vandē paśūnāṃ patim ।
vandē sūryaśaśāṅkavahninayanaṃ vandē mukundapriyaṃ
vandē bhaktajanāśrayaṃ cha varadaṃ vandē śivaṃ śaṅkaram ॥16॥

gātraṃ bhasmasitaṃ sitaṃ cha hasitaṃ hastē kapālaṃ sitaṃ var smitaṃ cha
khaṭvāṅgaṃ cha sitaṃ sitaścha vṛṣabhaḥ karṇē sitē kuṇḍalē ।
gaṅgā phēnasitā jaṭā paśupatēśchandraḥ sitō mūrdhani
sō'yaṃ sarvasitō dadātu vibhavaṃ pāpakṣayaṃ sarvadā ॥ 17॥

karacharaṇakṛtaṃ vākkāyajaṃ karmajaṃ vā
śravaṇanayanajaṃ vā mānasaṃ vā'parādham ।
vihitamavihitaṃ vā sarvamētatkṣmasva
śiva śiva karuṇābdhē śrīmahādēva śambhō ॥ 18॥

॥ iti śrīmad śaṅkarāchāryakṛta śivāparādhakṣamāpaṇastōtraṃ sampūrṇam ॥
id5_story.id5_9:
dēvarāja-sēvyamāna-pāvanāṅghri-paṅkajaṃ
vyāḻayajña-sūtramindu-śēkharaṃ kṛpākaram ।
nāradādi-yōgibṛnda-vanditaṃ digambaraṃ
kāśikāpurādhinātha kālabhairavaṃ bhajē ॥ 1 ॥

bhānukōṭi-bhāsvaraṃ bhavabdhitārakaṃ paraṃ
nīlakaṇṭha-mīpsitārtha-dāyakaṃ trilōchanam ।
kālakāla-mambujākṣa-makṣaśūla-makṣaraṃ
kāśikāpurādhinātha kālabhairavaṃ bhajē ॥ 2 ॥

śūlaṭaṅka-pāśadaṇḍa-pāṇimādi-kāraṇaṃ
śyāmakāya-mādidēva-makṣaraṃ nirāmayam ।
bhīmavikramaṃ prabhuṃ vichitra tāṇḍava priyaṃ
kāśikāpurādhinātha kālabhairavaṃ bhajē ॥ 3 ॥

bhukti-mukti-dāyakaṃ praśastachāru-vigrahaṃ
bhaktavatsalaṃ sthiraṃ samastalōka-vigraham । [sthitaṃ]
nikvaṇan-manōjña-hēma-kiṅkiṇī-lasatkaṭiṃ [vinikvaṇan]
kāśikāpurādhinātha kālabhairavaṃ bhajē ॥ 4 ॥

dharmasētu-pālakaṃ tvadharmamārga nāśakaṃ [nāśanaṃ]
karmapāśa-mōchakaṃ suśarma-dāyakaṃ vibhum ।
svarṇavarṇa-kēśapāśa-śōbhitāṅga-maṇḍalaṃ [śeṣapāśa, nirmalaṃ]
kāśikāpurādhinātha kālabhairavaṃ bhajē ॥ 5 ॥

ratna-pādukā-prabhābhirāma-pādayugmakaṃ
nitya-madvitīya-miṣṭa-daivataṃ nirañjanam ।
mṛtyudarpa-nāśanaṃ karāḻadaṃṣṭra-mōkṣadaṃ [bhūṣaṇaṃ]
kāśikāpurādhinātha kālabhairavaṃ bhajē ॥ 6 ॥

aṭṭahāsa-bhinna-padmajāṇḍakōśa-santatiṃ
dṛṣṭipāta-naṣṭapāpa-jālamugra-śāsanam ।
aṣṭasiddhi-dāyakaṃ kapālamālikā-dharaṃ
kāśikāpurādhinātha kālabhairavaṃ bhajē ॥ 7 ॥

bhūtasaṅgha-nāyakaṃ viśālakīrti-dāyakaṃ
kāśivāsi-lōka-puṇyapāpa-śōdhakaṃ vibhum । [kaśivāsa]
nītimārga-kōvidaṃ purātanaṃ jagatpatiṃ
kāśikāpurādhinātha kālabhairavaṃ bhajē ॥ 8 ॥

kālabhairavāṣṭakaṃ paṭhanti yē manōharaṃ
jñānamukti-sādhanaṃ vichitra-puṇya-vardhanam ।
śōkamōha-lōbhadainya-kōpatāpa-nāśanaṃ [dainyalōbha]
tē prayānti kālabhairavāṅghri-sannidhiṃ dhruvam ॥

iti śrīmatparamahaṃsaparivrājakācharyasya
śrīgōvindabhagavatpūjyapādaśiṣyasya
śrīmachChaṅkarabhagavataḥ kṛtau
śrī kālabhairavāṣṭakaṃ sampūrṇam ।
id5_story.id5_10:
prabhuṃ prāṇanāthaṃ vibhuṃ viśvanāthaṃ jagannātha nāthaṃ sadānanda bhājām ।
bhavadbhavya bhūtēśvaraṃ bhūtanāthaṃ, śivaṃ śaṅkaraṃ śambhu mīśānamīḍē ॥ 1 ॥

gaḻē ruṇḍamālaṃ tanau sarpajālaṃ mahākāla kālaṃ gaṇēśādi pālam ।
jaṭājūṭa gaṅgōttaraṅgairviśālaṃ, śivaṃ śaṅkaraṃ śambhu mīśānamīḍē ॥ 2॥

mudāmākaraṃ maṇḍanaṃ maṇḍayantaṃ mahā maṇḍalaṃ bhasma bhūṣādharaṃ tam ।
anādiṃ hyapāraṃ mahā mōhamāraṃ, śivaṃ śaṅkaraṃ śambhu mīśānamīḍē ॥ 3 ॥

vaṭādhō nivāsaṃ mahāṭṭāṭṭahāsaṃ mahāpāpa nāśaṃ sadā suprakāśam ।
girīśaṃ gaṇēśaṃ surēśaṃ mahēśaṃ, śivaṃ śaṅkaraṃ śambhu mīśānamīḍē ॥ 4 ॥

girīndrātmajā saṅgṛhītārdhadēhaṃ girau saṃsthitaṃ sarvadāpanna gēham ।
parabrahma brahmādibhir-vandyamānaṃ, śivaṃ śaṅkaraṃ śambhu mīśānamīḍē ॥ 5 ॥

kapālaṃ triśūlaṃ karābhyāṃ dadhānaṃ padāmbhōja namrāya kāmaṃ dadānam ।
balīvardhayānaṃ surāṇāṃ pradhānaṃ, śivaṃ śaṅkaraṃ śambhu mīśānamīḍē ॥ 6 ॥

śarachchandra gātraṃ gaṇānandapātraṃ trinētraṃ pavitraṃ dhanēśasya mitram ।
aparṇā kaḻatraṃ sadā sachcharitraṃ, śivaṃ śaṅkaraṃ śambhu mīśānamīḍē ॥ 7 ॥

haraṃ sarpahāraṃ chitā bhūvihāraṃ bhavaṃ vēdasāraṃ sadā nirvikāraṃ।
śmaśānē vasantaṃ manōjaṃ dahantaṃ, śivaṃ śaṅkaraṃ śambhu mīśānamīḍē ॥ 8 ॥

svayaṃ yaḥ prabhātē naraśśūla pāṇē paṭhēt stōtraratnaṃ tvihaprāpyaratnam ।
suputraṃ sudhānyaṃ sumitraṃ kaḻatraṃ vichitraissamārādhya mōkṣaṃ prayāti ॥
id5_story.id5_11:
namaḥ śivābhyāṃ navayauvanābhyāṃ
parasparāśliṣṭavapurdharābhyām ।
nagēndrakanyāvṛṣakētanābhyāṃ
namō namaḥ śaṅkarapārvatībhyām ॥ 1 ॥

namaḥ śivābhyāṃ sarasōtsavābhyāṃ
namaskṛtābhīṣṭavarapradābhyām ।
nārāyaṇēnārchitapādukābhyāṃ
namō namaḥ śaṅkarapārvatībhyām ॥ 2 ॥

namaḥ śivābhyāṃ vṛṣavāhanābhyāṃ
viriñchiviṣṇvindrasupūjitābhyām ।
vibhūtipāṭīravilēpanābhyāṃ
namō namaḥ śaṅkarapārvatībhyām ॥ 3 ॥

namaḥ śivābhyāṃ jagadīśvarābhyāṃ
jagatpatibhyāṃ jayavigrahābhyām ।
jambhārimukhyairabhivanditābhyāṃ
namō namaḥ śaṅkarapārvatībhyām ॥ 4 ॥

namaḥ śivābhyāṃ paramauṣadhābhyāṃ
pañchākṣarīpañjararañjitābhyām ।
prapañchasṛṣṭisthitisaṃhṛtābhyāṃ
namō namaḥ śaṅkarapārvatībhyām ॥ 5 ॥

namaḥ śivābhyāmatisundarābhyāṃ
atyantamāsaktahṛdambujābhyām ।
aśēṣalōkaikahitaṅkarābhyāṃ
namō namaḥ śaṅkarapārvatībhyām ॥ 6 ॥

namaḥ śivābhyāṃ kalināśanābhyāṃ
kaṅkāḻakalyāṇavapurdharābhyām ।
kailāsaśailasthitadēvatābhyāṃ
namō namaḥ śaṅkarapārvatībhyām ॥ 7 ॥

namaḥ śivābhyāmaśubhāpahābhyāṃ
aśēṣalōkaikaviśēṣitābhyām ।
akuṇṭhitābhyāṃ smṛtisambhṛtābhyāṃ
namō namaḥ śaṅkarapārvatībhyām ॥ 8 ॥

namaḥ śivābhyāṃ rathavāhanābhyāṃ
ravīnduvaiśvānaralōchanābhyām ।
rākāśaśāṅkābhamukhāmbujābhyāṃ
namō namaḥ śaṅkarapārvatībhyām ॥ 9 ॥

namaḥ śivābhyāṃ jaṭilandharābhyāṃ
jarāmṛtibhyāṃ cha vivarjitābhyām ।
janārdanābjōdbhavapūjitābhyāṃ
namō namaḥ śaṅkarapārvatībhyām ॥ 10 ॥

namaḥ śivābhyāṃ viṣamēkṣaṇābhyāṃ
bilvachChadāmallikadāmabhṛdbhyām ।
śōbhāvatīśāntavatīśvarābhyāṃ
namō namaḥ śaṅkarapārvatībhyām ॥ 11 ॥

namaḥ śivābhyāṃ paśupālakābhyāṃ
jagatrayīrakṣaṇabaddhahṛdbhyām ।
samastadēvāsurapūjitābhyāṃ
namō namaḥ śaṅkarapārvatībhyām ॥ 12 ॥

stōtraṃ trisandhyaṃ śivapārvatībhyāṃ
bhaktyā paṭhēddvādaśakaṃ narō yaḥ ।
sa sarvasaubhāgyaphalāni
bhuṅktē śatāyurāntē śivalōkamēti ॥ 13 ॥
id5_story.id5_12:
viditākhila śāstra sudhā jaladhē
mahitōpaniṣat-kathitārtha nidhē ।
hṛdayē kalayē vimalaṃ charaṇaṃ
bhava śaṅkara dēśika mē śaraṇam ॥ 1 ॥

karuṇā varuṇālaya pālaya māṃ
bhavasāgara duḥkha vidūna hṛdam ।
rachayākhila darśana tattvavidaṃ
bhava śaṅkara dēśika mē śaraṇam ॥ 2 ॥

bhavatā janatā suhitā bhavitā
nijabōdha vichāraṇa chārumatē ।
kalayēśvara jīva vivēka vidaṃ
bhava śaṅkara dēśika mē śaraṇam ॥ 3 ॥

bhava eva bhavāniti me nitarāṃ
samajāyata chētasi kautukitā ।
mama vāraya mōha mahājaladhiṃ
bhava śaṅkara dēśika mē śaraṇam ॥ 4 ॥

sukṛtē'dhikṛtē bahudhā bhavatō
bhavitā samadarśana lālasatā ।
ati dīnamimaṃ paripālaya māṃ
bhava śaṅkara dēśika mē śaraṇam ॥ 5 ॥

jagatīmavituṃ kalitākṛtayō
vicharanti mahāmāha sachChalataḥ ।
ahimāṃśurivātra vibhāsi gurō
bhava śaṅkara dēśika mē śaraṇam ॥ 6 ॥

gurupuṅgava puṅgavakētana tē
samatāmayatāṃ na hi kō'pi sudhīḥ ।
śaraṇāgata vatsala tattvanidhē
bhava śaṅkara dēśika mē śaraṇam ॥ 7 ॥

viditā na mayā viśadaika kalā
na cha kiñchana kāñchanamasti gurō ।
dṛtamēva vidhēhi kṛpāṃ sahajāṃ
bhava śaṅkara dēśika mē śaraṇam ॥ 8 ॥
id5_story.id5_13:
ratnaiḥ kalpitamāsanaṃ himajalaiḥ snānaṃ cha divyāmbaraṃ
nānāratna vibhūṣitaṃ mṛgamadāmōdāṅkitaṃ chandanam ।
jātī champaka bilvapatra rachitaṃ puṣpaṃ cha dhūpaṃ tathā
dīpaṃ dēva dayānidhē paśupatē hṛtkalpitaṃ gṛhyatām ॥ 1 ॥

sauvarṇē navaratnakhaṇḍa rachitē pātrē ghṛtaṃ pāyasaṃ
bhakṣyaṃ pañchavidhaṃ payōdadhiyutaṃ rambhāphalaṃ pānakam ।
śākānāmayutaṃ jalaṃ ruchikaraṃ karpūra khaṇḍōjjvalaṃ
tāmbūlaṃ manasā mayā virachitaṃ bhaktyā prabhō svīkuru ॥ 2 ॥

Chatraṃ chāmarayōryugaṃ vyajanakaṃ chādarśakaṃ nirmalaṃ
vīṇā bhēri mṛdaṅga kāhalakalā gītaṃ cha nṛtyaṃ tathā ।
sāṣṭāṅgaṃ praṇatiḥ stuti-rbahuvidhā-hyētat-samastaṃ mayā
saṅkalpēna samarpitaṃ tava vibhō pūjāṃ gṛhāṇa prabhō ॥ 3 ॥

ātmā tvaṃ girijā matiḥ sahacharāḥ prāṇāḥ śarīraṃ gṛhaṃ
pūjā tē viṣayōpabhōga-rachanā nidrā samādhisthitiḥ ।
sañchāraḥ padayōḥ pradakṣiṇavidhiḥ stōtrāṇi sarvā girō
yadyatkarma karōmi tattadakhilaṃ śambhō tavārādhanam ॥ 4 ॥

kara charaṇa kṛtaṃ vākkāyajaṃ karmajaṃ vā
śravaṇa nayanajaṃ vā mānasaṃ vāparādham ।
vihitamavihitaṃ vā sarvamētat-kṣamasva
jaya jaya karuṇābdhē śrī mahādēva śambhō ॥ 5 ॥
id5_story.id5_14:
ōṃ namaḥ śivāya śivāya namaḥ ōṃ
ōṃ namaḥ śivāya śivāya namaḥ ōṃ

nāgēndrahārāya trilōchanāya
bhasmāṅgarāgāya mahēśvarāya ।
nityāya śuddhāya digambarāya
tasmai "na" kārāya namaḥ śivāya ॥ 1 ॥

mandākinī salila chandana charchitāya
nandīśvara pramathanātha mahēśvarāya ।
mandāra mukhya bahupuṣpa supūjitāya
tasmai "ma" kārāya namaḥ śivāya ॥ 2 ॥

śivāya gaurī vadanābja bṛnda
sūryāya dakṣādhvara nāśakāya ।
śrī nīlakaṇṭhāya vṛṣabhadhvajāya
tasmai "śi" kārāya namaḥ śivāya ॥ 3 ॥

vasiṣṭha kumbhōdbhava gautamārya
munīndra dēvārchita śēkharāya ।
chandrārka vaiśvānara lōchanāya
tasmai "va" kārāya namaḥ śivāya ॥ 4 ॥

yajña-svarūpāya jaṭādharāya [yakṣa-]
pināka hastāya sanātanāya ।
divyāya dēvāya digambarāya
tasmai "ya" kārāya namaḥ śivāya ॥ 5 ॥

pañchākṣaramidaṃ puṇyaṃ yaḥ paṭhēchChiva sannidhau ।
śivalōkamavāpnōti śivēna saha mōdatē ॥
id5_story.id5_15:
śrīgaṇēśāya namaḥ ।
ōṃ asya śrīmahāmṛtyuñjayastōtramantrasya śrī mārkaṇḍēya ṛṣiḥ,
anuṣṭupChandaḥ, śrīmṛtyuñjayō dēvatā, gaurī śaktiḥ,
mama sarvāriṣṭasamastamṛtyuśāntyarthaṃ sakalaiśvaryaprāptyarthaṃ
japē vinōyōgaḥ ।

dhyānam
chandrārkāgnivilōchanaṃ smitamukhaṃ padmadvayāntasthitaṃ
mudrāpāśamṛgākṣasatravilasatpāṇiṃ himāṃśuprabham ।
kōṭīndupragalatsudhāplutatamuṃ hārādibhūṣōjjvalaṃ
kāntaṃ viśvavimōhanaṃ paśupatiṃ mṛtyuñjayaṃ bhāvayēt ॥

rudraṃ paśupatiṃ sthāṇuṃ nīlakaṇṭhamumāpatim ।
namāmi śirasā dēvaṃ kiṃ nō mṛtyuḥ kariṣyati ॥ 1॥

nīlakaṇṭhaṃ kālamūrttiṃ kālajñaṃ kālanāśanam ।
namāmi śirasā dēvaṃ kiṃ nō mṛtyuḥ kariṣyati ॥ 2॥

nīlakaṇṭhaṃ virūpākṣaṃ nirmalaṃ nilayapradam ।
namāmi śirasā dēvaṃ kiṃ nō mṛtyuḥ kariṣyati ॥ 3॥

vāmadēvaṃ mahādēvaṃ lōkanāthaṃ jagadgurum ।
namāmi śirasā dēvaṃ kiṃ nō mṛtyuḥ kariṣyati ॥ 4॥

dēvadēvaṃ jagannāthaṃ dēvēśaṃ vṛṣabhadhvajam ।
namāmi śirasā dēvaṃ kiṃ nō mṛtyuḥ kariṣyati ॥ 5॥

tryakṣaṃ chaturbhujaṃ śāntaṃ jaṭāmakuṭadhāriṇam ।
namāmi śirasā dēvaṃ kiṃ nō mṛtyuḥ kariṣyati ॥ 6॥

bhasmōddhūlitasarvāṅgaṃ nāgābharaṇabhūṣitam ।
namāmi śirasā dēvaṃ kiṃ nō mṛtyuḥ kariṣyati ॥ 7॥

anantamavyayaṃ śāntaṃ akṣamālādharaṃ haram ।
namāmi śirasā dēvaṃ kiṃ nō mṛtyuḥ kariṣyati ॥ 8॥

ānandaṃ paramaṃ nityaṃ kaivalyapadadāyinam ।
namāmi śirasā dēvaṃ kiṃ nō mṛtyuḥ kariṣyati ॥ 9॥

arddhanārīśvaraṃ dēvaṃ pārvatīprāṇanāyakam ।
namāmi śirasā dēvaṃ kiṃ nō mṛtyuḥ kariṣyati ॥ 10॥

pralayasthitikarttāramādikarttāramīśvaram ।
namāmi śirasā dēvaṃ kiṃ nō mṛtyuḥ kariṣyati ॥ 11॥

vyōmakēśaṃ virūpākṣaṃ chandrārddhakṛtaśēkharam ।
namāmi śirasā dēvaṃ kiṃ nō mṛtyuḥ kariṣyati ॥ 12॥

gaṅgādharaṃ śaśidharaṃ śaṅkaraṃ śūlapāṇinam ।
(pāṭhabhēdaḥ) gaṅgādharaṃ mahādēvaṃ sarvābharaṇabhūṣitam ।
namāmi śirasā dēvaṃ kiṃ nō mṛtyuḥ kariṣyati ॥ 13॥

anāthaḥ paramānantaṃ kaivalyapadagāmini ।
namāmi śirasā dēvaṃ kiṃ nō mṛtyuḥ kariṣyati ॥ 14॥

svargāpavargadātāraṃ sṛṣṭisthityantakāraṇam ।
namāmi śirasā dēvaṃ kiṃ nō mṛtyuḥ kariṣyati ॥ 15॥

kalpāyurddēhi mē puṇyaṃ yāvadāyurarōgatām ।
namāmi śirasā dēvaṃ kiṃ nō mṛtyuḥ kariṣyati ॥ 16॥

śivēśānāṃ mahādēvaṃ vāmadēvaṃ sadāśivam ।
namāmi śirasā dēvaṃ kiṃ nō mṛtyuḥ kariṣyati ॥ 17॥

utpattisthitisaṃhārakartāramīśvaraṃ gurum ।
namāmi śirasā dēvaṃ kiṃ nō mṛtyuḥ kariṣyati ॥ 18॥

phalaśruti
mārkaṇḍēyakṛtaṃ stōtraṃ yaḥ paṭhēchChivasannidhau ।
tasya mṛtyubhayaṃ nāsti nāgnichaurabhayaṃ kvachit ॥ 19॥

śatāvarttaṃ prakartavyaṃ saṅkaṭē kaṣṭanāśanam ।
śuchirbhūtvā pathētstōtraṃ sarvasiddhipradāyakam ॥ 20॥

mṛtyuñjaya mahādēva trāhi māṃ śaraṇāgatam ।
janmamṛtyujarārōgaiḥ pīḍitaṃ karmabandhanaiḥ ॥ 21॥

tāvakastvadgataḥ prāṇastvachchittō'haṃ sadā mṛḍa ।
iti vijñāpya dēvēśaṃ tryambakākhyamanuṃ japēt ॥ 23॥

namaḥ śivāya sāmbāya harayē paramātmanē ।
praṇataklēśanāśāya yōgināṃ patayē namaḥ ॥ 24॥

śatāṅgāyurmantraḥ ।
ōṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ hraiṃ hraḥ
hana hana daha daha pacha pacha gṛhāṇa gṛhāṇa
māraya māraya mardaya mardaya mahāmahābhairava bhairavarūpēṇa
dhunaya dhunaya kampaya kampaya vighnaya vighnaya viśvēśvara
kṣōbhaya kṣōbhaya kaṭukaṭu mōhaya mōhaya huṃ phaṭ
svāhā iti mantramātrēṇa samābhīṣṭō bhavati ॥

॥ iti śrīmārkaṇḍēyapurāṇē mārkaṇḍēyakṛta mahāmṛtyuñjayastōtraṃ
sampūrṇam ॥
id5_story.id5_16:
saurāṣṭrē sōmanādhañcha śrīśailē mallikārjunam ।
ujjayinyāṃ mahākālaṃ ōṅkārētvamāmalēśvaram ॥
parlyāṃ vaidyanādhañcha ḍhākinyāṃ bhīma śaṅkaram ।
sētubandhētu rāmēśaṃ nāgēśaṃ dārukāvanē ॥
vāraṇāśyāntu viśvēśaṃ trayambakaṃ gautamītaṭē ।
himālayētu kēdāraṃ ghṛṣṇēśantu viśālakē ॥

ētāni jyōtirliṅgāni sāyaṃ prātaḥ paṭhēnnaraḥ ।
sapta janma kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ smaraṇēna vinaśyati ॥

id7.id7_1: Har Har Mahadev — Just His Name Is Enough to Lift the Burden of the World.
id7.id7_2: Where Bholenath's Hand Is Upon You, Even Destiny Bows Down.
id7.id7_3: Shiva Means Peace, Shiva Means Strength, Shiva Means Complete Surrender.
id7.id7_4: Why Fear? Mahadev's Hand Is Upon Me.
id7.id7_5: He Drank Poison Yet Never Lost His Smile — That Is Mahadev.
id7.id7_6: If Your Devotion Is True, Bholenath Never Forgets You.
id7.id7_7: No One Leaves Mahadev's Abode Empty-Handed.
id7.id7_8: Take Shiva's Name, and Sorrow Will Automatically Feel Smaller.
id7.id7_9: Every Battle of Life Becomes Easier When Your Faith Is in Shiva.
id7.id7_10: Om Namah Shivaya — The Entire Universe Is Contained Within These Five Syllables.
id7.id7_11: Mahadev Gives Time, But Never Injustice.
id7.id7_12: A Shiva Devotee Does Not Need the World's Recognition.
id7.id7_13: One Who Attains Shiva Is Rich Even After Losing Everything Else.
id7.id7_14: Bholenath Is Innocent, But Never Weak.
id7.id7_15: Trust Mahadev; He Will Take Care of Everything Else.
id7.id7_16: Shiva's Grace May Come Late, But It Is Never Incomplete.
id7.id7_17: Even If the Whole World Stands Against You, Do Not Worry — Mahadev Is With You.
id7.id7_18: Shiva Is Not the End; Shiva Is Infinite.
id7.id7_19: Those Who Have Found Mahadev No Longer Need to Complain.
id7.id7_20: Only Mahadev Knows How to Heal a Broken Heart.
id7.id7_21: Even Time Takes Notice of a Devotee of Mahakal.
id7.id7_22: Devotion to Shiva Is Not About Showing Off; It Is About Immersing Yourself Completely.
id7.id7_23: Have Faith — Shiva Is Never Late.
id7.id7_24: Bowing Before Mahadev Is Not Defeat; It Is the Greatest Victory.
id7.id7_25: Want to Change Your Life? Chant 'Om Namah Shivaya' Once with a True Heart.
id7.id7_26: You Do Not Need to Ask Shiva for Anything; You Only Need to Remember Him.
id7.id7_27: A Devotee of Bholenath Never Sells Their Self-Respect.
id7.id7_28: Mahadev Belongs to Everyone, But He Is Even Closer to Those Who Call Upon Him.
id7.id7_29: Shiva Is the Peace That Remains Even in the Middle of a Storm.
id7.id7_30: Nandi's Patience and Shiva's Strength — Both Are Worth Learning From.
id7.id7_31: No One Can Defeat One Whom Mahadev Protects.
id7.id7_32: Ego Cannot Stand Before Shiva's Trident.
id7.id7_33: The World Changes, But Mahadev's Grace Does Not.
id7.id7_34: Devote Yourself to Shiva — The Fruits Will Come Without Asking.
id7.id7_35: When the Mind Is Restless, Shiva's Name Is the Greatest Remedy.
id7.id7_36: Mahadev Says — Keep Moving, I Will Show You the Way.
id7.id7_37: Where There Is Devotion, There Is Bholenath; the Temple Is Only an Excuse.
id7.id7_38: Shiva Remains Steady in the Cremation Ground and in Heaven — That Is True Meditation.
id7.id7_39: Learn to Digest Life's Poison; That Is What Mahadev Taught Us.
id7.id7_40: Bholenath Sees a Devotee's Feelings, Not Their Offerings.
id7.id7_41: Even One Bilva Leaf Is Enough When the Heart Is Pure.
id7.id7_42: Cry Before Mahadev, Then Keep Smiling Before the World.
id7.id7_43: A Shiva Devotee Is Known Not by Their Tilak, But by Their Character.
id7.id7_45: Shiva Is the Truth That Never Changes.
id7.id7_46: Taking Bholenath's Name Makes Half the Fear Melt Away.
id7.id7_47: Leave It to Mahadev — He Will Do It Better Than You Can.
id7.id7_48: After Going to Shiva, There Is No Need to Complain About Destiny.
id7.id7_49: Practice, Be Patient — Shiva Tests You, But Never Abandons You.
id7.id7_50: One Who Belongs to Mahadev Is No Longer a Slave to the World.
id7.id7_51: In Devotion to Shiva, Silence Speaks More Than Words.
id7.id7_52: Ganga in His Locks, the Moon on His Head, Poison in His Throat — Yet a Smile on His Face. That Is Mahadev.
id7.id7_53: Remember Shiva, and Ego Will Melt Away on Its Own.
id7.id7_54: One Who Has Bholenath Has Everything.
id7.id7_55: Mahadev May Let His Devotee Fall, But He Never Lets Them Break.
id7.id7_56: Shiva Says — Do Your Work, I Will Take Care of the Result.
id7.id7_57: When Devotion Is Strong, Even Destiny Can Change.
id7.id7_58: Shiva Is the Home Where a Tired Mind Finds Rest.
id7.id7_59: A Devotee of Mahadev Never Runs Out of Confidence.
id7.id7_60: Listen to the Sound of the Damru — It Holds the Rhythm of the Entire Universe.
id7.id7_61: Shiva Is Simple, and That Is Why He Is the Greatest.
id7.id7_62: As Long as There Is Breath, There Will Be 'Har Har Mahadev'.
id7.id7_63: Mahadev Forgives His Devotee's Mistakes, But Never Forgets Their Devotion.
id7.id7_64: Age, Caste, or Status Cannot Stand in the Way of Devotion to Shiva.
id7.id7_65: Where Shiva Resides in the Mind, Peace Resides in Life.
id7.id7_66: When You Bow Before Shiva, Your Destiny Rises.
id7.id7_67: Bholenath Never Leaves His Devotee Alone.
id7.id7_68: Mahadev Is Not the Destination; He Is the Entire Journey.
id7.id7_69: A Shiva Devotee Does Not Fear, Because They Are a Devotee of the Lord of Death.
id7.id7_70: When Life Is Dark, Shiva's Name Becomes a Lamp.
id7.id7_71: When Mahadev Showers His Grace, Nothing More Remains to Be Asked For.
id7.id7_72: Shiva Is Not Destruction; Shiva Is a New Beginning.
id7.id7_73: Do Not Fear When the Old Breaks — Mahadev Is Creating Something New.
id7.id7_74: Devotion to Shiva Is Not Fashion; It Is a Way of Life.
id7.id7_75: Excuses Do Not Work Before Bholenath; Only Pure Feelings Matter.
id7.id7_76: Mahadev Is the Greatest Giver, Yet He Himself Is the Simplest.
id7.id7_77: There Is Poison in Shiva's Throat, Yet He Is Called the Benevolent One — That Is Sacrifice.
id7.id7_78: When Faith Is Unwavering, Shiva Can Manifest Even from Stone.
id7.id7_79: Mahadev Counts His Devotee's Tears, Not Their Words.
id7.id7_80: Build a Bond with Shiva — All Other Relationships Will Become Easier.
id7.id7_81: One Who Has Mahakal's Support Has Nothing to Fear from Time.
id7.id7_82: Devotion to Shiva Calms the Mind and Strengthens the Heart.
id7.id7_83: Trusting Bholenath Is the Safest Investment.
id7.id7_84: Mahadev's Name Holds the Power to Turn Even Defeat Around.
id7.id7_85: Shiva Says — Remember Me, and I Will Take Care of the Rest.
id7.id7_86: A Shiva Devotee Is Humble, But Never Helpless.
id7.id7_87: Ego Must Be Left Outside Before Entering Mahadev's Door.
id7.id7_88: Shiva Is the Strength That Is Born from Peace.
